title: The two workhorses: hM3Dq and hM4Di
objective: Choose between hM3Dq and hM4Di based on whether you want to excite or silence, and explain the G-protein mechanism of each.

steps.title: Two receptors, opposite jobs
steps.body:
Most experiments use one of two [[DREADD|DREADDs]]:

- **[[hM3Dq]]** — couples to **Gq**. Activation drives the cell toward **firing** (excitatory).
- **[[hM4Di]]** — couples to **Gi/o**. Activation **silences** the cell (inhibitory).

Same drug can be used for both; the receptor decides the direction.

visual.alt: The same drug is applied to two neurons; the hM3Dq neuron fires more while the hM4Di neuron goes quiet.
visual.caption: Same drug, opposite effect — hM3Dq excites, hM4Di silences.

steps.title: Why Gq excites
steps.body: **hM3Dq → Gq → phospholipase C → IP₃/DAG and intracellular Ca²⁺ release**, with depolarizing effects that raise excitability. In practice, activating hM3Dq makes neurons more likely to fire, which is why it's used to drive a population and read out the behavioral or physiological consequence.

flag.note: The exact downstream currents vary by cell type; 'Gq → more excitable' is the working summary.

steps.title: Why Gi silences
steps.body: **hM4Di → Gi/o** does two useful things: it **inhibits adenylyl cyclase** and, importantly, activates **GIRK potassium channels** (hyperpolarizing the cell) and **suppresses neurotransmitter release at the terminal**. So hM4Di can both quiet the cell body and dampen its output.

steps.prompt: Match each DREADD to its mechanism and effect.
pairs: Gq-coupled → raises excitability → neurons fire more
Gi/o-coupled → GIRK/K⁺ + less release → neurons silenced
steps.explanation: Direction of the effect is set by which G protein the engineered receptor recruits.

steps.prompt: Your hypothesis is that pancreas-innervating sensory neurons SUPPRESS insulin release. You want to test necessity by shutting those neurons down during a glucose challenge. Which DREADD fits?
steps.explanation: To remove the neurons' contribution (a loss-of-function / necessity test), you silence them — hM4Di. hM3Dq would instead test sufficiency by driving them.

variants.setup: You hypothesize that pancreas-innervating sensory neurons suppress insulin release, and you'll test it by removing their activity.
variants.reveal: To test a suppressive role by loss-of-function, silence the neurons with hM4Di and watch insulin.

steps.setup: You express hM3Dq in a neuron population and give the [[actuator]]. To confirm the neurons were actually driven, you stain for the immediate-early gene [[c-Fos]].
steps.prompt: What do you predict in the DREADD-expressing neurons vs. neighbors?
options: More c-Fos in the DREADD+ neurons than in their neighbors
Less c-Fos in the DREADD+ neurons than in their neighbors
Equal c-Fos everywhere, in DREADD+ cells and neighbors alike
steps.reveal: c-Fos rises in recently-active neurons, so hM3Dq+ cells should show more than non-expressing neighbors. This is a common way to confirm the activation DREADD fired (a 'manipulation check' — more in C5-L5).

variants.prompt: After exciting DREADD+ neurons, how should c-Fos compare in DREADD+ cells versus their neighbors?
options: More c-Fos in the DREADD+ neurons
Less c-Fos in the DREADD+ neurons
variants.explanation: c-Fos marks recently active neurons, so an excitatory DREADD should raise it selectively in DREADD+ cells — a manipulation check.
